natural: lay the foundations and start the enterprise

meaning.en: To found a dynasty, state or major enterprise from scratch.
meaning.zh: 开创基业，创建事业，多指建立王朝或大业。

equivalents: lay the foundations of an empire

examples.zh: 这位开基创业的君主为后世打下了根基。
examples.en: This ruler, who founded the dynasty from nothing, laid the groundwork for later generations.

examples.zh: 老一辈开基创业，我们要守住这份家业。
examples.en: The older generation built the business from scratch; we must hold on to it.

usage.en: Used of founding a state, dynasty or great undertaking; formal, written style.
usage.zh: 多用于创建王朝、国家或大事业，书面语。

natural: talent beyond others

meaning.en: Having literary or artistic gifts far beyond ordinary people.
meaning.zh: 才华和气质超过一般人。

examples.zh: 这位青年作家才气过人，一出手就惊艳文坛。
examples.en: This young writer is exceptionally gifted and stunned the literary world with his debut.

examples.zh: 她才气过人，却从不张扬。
examples.en: She is remarkably talented, yet never shows off.

usage.en: Praises creative talent, especially in writing or art; predicate or attributive. A set phrase rather than a classical idiom.
usage.zh: 称赞文艺方面的才华；多作谓语、定语。属固定词组。

natural: wheel the horse and draw the bow

meaning.en: To pose threateningly as if about to shoot without releasing the arrow; to hold back while appearing ready to act.
meaning.zh: 骑着马盘旋，拉满了弓却不发箭，比喻故作姿态、引而不发。

examples.zh: 他盘马弯弓，摆足了架势，却迟迟不出手。
examples.en: He wheeled and drew his bow, striking every pose but never loosing the arrow.

examples.zh: 对手盘马弯弓，其实是在试探我们的底线。
examples.en: The opponent is only feinting, testing our bottom line.

story.en: Han Yu's poem on a pheasant shot with an arrow has the line 'drawing the bow and wheeling the horse, he holds back from shooting' (弯弓盘马惜不发).
story.zh: 韩愈《雉带箭》：“将军欲以巧伏人，盘马弯弓惜不发。”

usage.en: Describes a show of readiness while holding back; can also mean drawing out suspense. Often paired with 引而不发.
usage.zh: 形容摆出架势而不行动，也可指故意制造悬念；常与“引而不发”同用。

natural: spread wide and raise high

meaning.en: Originally, writing in an ornate, sweeping, grandiose style; now also lavish display for show.
meaning.zh: 原指文辞铺陈夸张、气势宏大；后也指过分讲究排场。

examples.zh: 这篇赋铺张扬厉，极尽辞藻之美。
examples.en: This rhapsody is sweeping and ornate, a feast of fine diction.

examples.zh: 婚礼铺张扬厉，花了不少钱。
examples.en: The wedding was lavish and showy, and cost a great deal.

usage.en: In literary criticism it may be neutral or mildly approving; of events or spending it usually implies excess.
usage.zh: 用于评论文章时中性或略带褒义；用于排场花费时多含过度之意。

natural: a befuddled old schoolmaster

meaning.en: A pedantic, muddle-headed old scholar who knows his books but little of the world.
meaning.zh: 指迂腐浅陋、思想糊涂的读书人。

examples.zh: 别听那位冬烘先生的，他根本不懂现在的行情。
examples.en: Don't listen to that fusty old pedant; he knows nothing about the market today.

examples.zh: 他被同学笑称冬烘先生，因为凡事都要引经据典。
examples.en: Classmates call him a stuffy old pedant because he quotes the classics for everything.

story.en: The Tang examiner Zheng Xun, careless and befuddled, was said to have mistaken Yan Biao for a descendant of Yan Zhenqing; a ditty mocked him as 'muddled'.
story.zh: 唐代郑薰主持科考，误以颜标为颜真卿之后，时人讥其“冬烘”，后称迂腐糊涂的读书人为冬烘先生。

usage.en: Mocking; usually a noun for a person. Note 烘 is read hōng here, not hóng.
usage.zh: 带讽刺意味，多指人；注意“烘”读 hōng。

natural: a brocade heart and embroidered mouth

meaning.en: Having beautiful thoughts and eloquent words; a gift for fine writing.
meaning.zh: 心思如锦，言辞如绣，形容文思优美、辞藻华丽。

equivalents: a heart of silk and a tongue of gold

examples.zh: 她锦心绣口，一篇文章写得字字珠玑。
examples.en: With her brilliant mind and polished prose, every word of her essay is a gem.

examples.zh: 这位诗人锦心绣口，满腹锦绣文章。
examples.en: The poet has a beautiful mind and a beautiful tongue, full of splendid writing.

story.en: Liu Zongyuan's 'Prayer for Skill' says of fine parallel prose: '锦心绣口' (a brocade heart, an embroidered mouth).
story.zh: 柳宗元《乞巧文》：“骈四俪六，锦心绣口。”

usage.en: Praise for a writer's mind and expression; literary register.
usage.zh: 赞美文人思想与辞章，书面语。

literal: steal · state · one who · become marquis
natural: he who steals a state becomes a lord

meaning.en: Petty thieves are punished, but those who seize a whole state are honoured as rulers; a lament at unjust power.
meaning.zh: 偷国家的人反而封侯称王，讽刺社会不公、强权者逍遥法外。

equivalents: steal a hook and be hanged, steal a country and be crowned

examples.zh: 窃钩者诛，窃国者侯，这世道真不公平。
examples.en: Steal a hook and you are executed, steal a state and you are made a lord; how unjust the world is.

examples.zh: 历史上窃国者侯的事不胜枚举。
examples.en: History is full of cases where those who seized states were rewarded.

story.en: Zhuangzi writes that one who steals a belt-hook is executed, while one who steals a state becomes a lord; Sima Qian repeats it in the 'Biographies of Knights-errant'.
story.zh: 《庄子·胠箧》：“彼窃钩者诛，窃国者为诸侯。”《史记·游侠列传》：“窃钩者诛，窃国者侯。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Usually quoted with the first half 窃钩者诛; criticises double standards of justice.
usage.zh: 常与上句“窃钩者诛”连用，批评法律不公、对强者宽容。

natural: hang up one's official cap and leave

meaning.en: To resign from office, often in protest or disillusionment.
meaning.zh: 把官帽挂起来离开，指辞官而去。

equivalents: hang up one's hat and quit

examples.zh: 他看不惯官场作风，毅然挂冠而去。
examples.en: Disgusted with the ways of officialdom, he resolutely resigned.

examples.zh: 总经理一怒之下挂冠而去，让公司措手不及。
examples.en: The managing director stormed out and resigned, catching the firm off guard.

story.en: Feng Meng, angered by Wang Mang's killing of his own son, took off his cap, hung it on the east gate of the capital and left office.
story.zh: 《后汉书·逢萌传》：王莽杀其子宇，逢萌说“三纲绝矣”，“即解冠挂东都城门，归，将家属浮海，客于辽东”。

usage.en: Often implies a principled or disenchanted resignation; literary, sometimes used playfully in modern business contexts.
usage.zh: 多含出于操守或失望而辞职之意；书面语，现代也偶用于商界。

natural: the roc spreads its wings

meaning.en: To launch a great career or soar toward lofty ambitions, like the mythical Peng bird taking flight.
meaning.zh: 像传说中的大鹏展开翅膀，比喻前程远大、抱负宏伟。

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长祝福大家鲲鹏展翅，前程万里。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the head wished everyone a soaring future.

examples.zh: 新公司上市，正如鲲鹏展翅，前景广阔。
examples.en: With its listing, the new company is taking off, its prospects wide open.

story.en: Zhuangzi tells of a huge fish, Kun, that turns into the bird Peng, whose wings are like clouds hanging across the sky and which rises ninety thousand li.
story.zh: 《庄子·逍遥游》：“北冥有鱼，其名为鲲……化而为鸟，其名为鹏……怒而飞，其翼若垂天之云。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Used in blessings and praise for ambitious beginnings; not a classical four-character fixed form, but a common set phrase.
usage.zh: 多用于祝愿或赞美起步远大；属常见固定词组。

natural: on the other side of the water

meaning.en: Someone or something longed for but out of reach, as if across a river.
meaning.zh: 在水的另一边，形容所思慕的人或事物近在眼前而难以接近。

examples.zh: 她就像在水一方的伊人，可望而不可即。
examples.en: She was like the one across the water, seen but never reached.

examples.zh: 理想在水一方，我们仍要溯流而上。
examples.en: Our dream lies across the river, yet we must still press upstream.

story.en: The Book of Songs poem 'Reeds' says: 'The one I long for is on the other side of the water.'
story.zh: 《蒹葭》：“蒹葭苍苍，白露为霜。所谓伊人，在水一方。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Poetic image of longing; often cited with 伊人 (the one I long for). Not for literal location.
usage.zh: 表达思慕的诗意说法；常与“伊人”连用，不指实际方位。

natural: lamplight growing faint

meaning.en: Lights dimming or sparse as night wears on; also the quiet, out-of-the-way spot where one finally finds what one sought.
meaning.zh: 灯光稀疏黯淡的样子，也借指夜深冷清处，常暗含“蓦然回首”的意味。

examples.zh: 夜深了，街头灯火阑珊，行人寥寥。
examples.en: Late at night the street lamps were dim and few people were about.

examples.zh: 他在灯火阑珊处终于找到了那家老书店。
examples.en: He finally found the old bookshop where the lights glimmered faintly.

story.en: Xin Qiji's lantern-festival poem ends: 'I searched for her a thousand times in the crowd; suddenly turning my head, there she stood where the lamplight was dim.'
story.zh: 辛弃疾《青玉案·元夕》：“众里寻他千百度，蓦然回首，那人却在，灯火阑珊处。”

usage.en: Often quoted from Xin Qiji's poem, as a symbol of quietly finding what one longed for. Read 阑珊 as lán shān.
usage.zh: 常引自辛弃疾词，象征于不经意间寻得所求；“阑珊”读 lán shān。

natural: half a copy of the Analects

meaning.en: A little real learning, applied well, is enough to govern with; used to praise the practical value of the classics.
meaning.zh: 只需半部《论语》便能治天下，比喻读书要精、要用得上。

equivalents: a little learning put to use

examples.zh: 赵普半部论语治天下，说明学贵在用。
examples.en: Zhao Pu ruled with half the Analects, which shows that what matters is how learning is used.

examples.zh: 他常说半部论语足以做人处世。
examples.en: He often says that half the Analects is enough to guide one's conduct.

story.en: Song chief minister Zhao Pu was said to have read little beyond the Analects, yet remarked that half of it had helped Taizu win the empire and the other half would help Taizong keep it in peace.
story.zh: 宋代赵普读书不多，曾说：“臣有《论语》一部，以半部佐太祖定天下，以半部佐陛下致太平。”

usage.en: Often quoted in the full form 半部论语治天下; praises depth over breadth, sometimes also self-deprecating about one's reading.
usage.zh: 常引全句“半部论语治天下”；强调精读与致用，也可作自谦读书不多。

natural: pound the chest and weep blood

meaning.en: To grieve with extreme anguish, especially over a parent's death or a great misfortune.
meaning.zh: 捶打胸口，哭得泣出血来，形容极度悲痛。

examples.zh: 母亲去世，他椎心泣血，几度昏厥。
examples.en: When his mother died he was crushed with grief and fainted several times.

examples.zh: 面对灾难中的亡者，全国人民椎心泣血。
examples.en: The whole nation mourned the dead of the disaster with deep anguish.

story.en: Li Ling's famous letter to Su Wu, written in exile, uses the phrase 'beat the heart and weep blood' for his anguish.
story.zh: 李陵《答苏武书》中有“椎心而泣血”之语，写自己的悲痛。

date.en: Western Han, 1st c. BC (attributed; authenticity doubtful)

usage.en: Very strong, formal expression of grief. Written 椎 (chuí, to strike); the form 锥心泣血 is a common variant.
usage.zh: 表示极度悲痛，语气强烈，多用于书面；“椎”读 chuí，也作“锥心泣血”。

natural: a gallon of wine, a hundred poems

meaning.en: Remarkable poetic talent that pours out poem after poem under the influence of wine.
meaning.zh: 喝一斗酒能作百首诗，形容诗才敏捷、豪放。

equivalents: a hundred poems from a jug of wine

examples.zh: 人说李白斗酒百篇，下笔如有神。
examples.en: They say Li Bai wrote a hundred poems on a gallon of wine, his brush as if inspired.

examples.zh: 这位诗人豪饮善吟，有斗酒百篇之称。
examples.en: This poet, a hearty drinker and gifted improviser, was known for his hundred poems on a jug of wine.

story.en: Du Fu's 'Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup' describes Li Bai: 'Li Bai, a gallon of wine and a hundred poems.'
story.zh: 杜甫《饮中八仙歌》：“李白斗酒诗百篇，长安市上酒家眠。”

usage.en: Associated with Li Bai; praises quick inspiration and bold personality. Here 斗 is dǒu, a measure of wine.
usage.zh: 多与李白相关，称赞才思敏捷、性格豪放；“斗”读 dǒu。

natural: piles of gold, heaps of jade

meaning.en: Immense accumulated wealth.
meaning.zh: 金玉堆积如山，形容财富极多。

examples.zh: 他家堆金积玉，却从不显摆。
examples.en: His family is immensely rich, yet never shows it off.

examples.zh: 堆金积玉也买不来健康。
examples.en: All the gold and jade in the world cannot buy health.

usage.en: Can describe wealth neutrally or imply that wealth is not everything.
usage.zh: 可中性形容财富，也常用来强调“钱不是万能”。

literal: content with · the usual · dwell in · the smooth
natural: settle in the ordinary and live with the smooth

meaning.en: To be content with one's ordinary lot and accept circumstances calmly.
meaning.zh: 安于常态，顺应环境，不求改变。

examples.zh: 他安常处顺，从不与人争。
examples.en: He takes life as it comes and never competes with others.

examples.zh: 安常处顺固然平静，但也可能错过机会。
examples.en: Settling for the ordinary is peaceful, but it may mean missing opportunities.

usage.en: Can be praise for composure or mild criticism of lack of drive, depending on context. 处 here is chǔ.
usage.zh: 可褒指从容淡定，亦可贬指不思进取；“处”读 chǔ。

natural: uproot the base and block the source

meaning.en: Originally, to destroy the root cause of something; now often used for thoroughly abolishing, or for destroying the very foundations.
meaning.zh: 拔掉树根，堵住水源，比喻根除祸患；也指破坏根基。

examples.zh: 要治理污染必须拔本塞源，不能头痛医头。
examples.en: To fight pollution we must tackle the root cause, not just treat symptoms.

examples.zh: 拔本塞源的做法会让传统行业彻底消失。
examples.en: A policy that destroys the foundations will make the traditional trade vanish altogether.

story.en: In the Zuo Zhuan an envoy warns that discarding one's trusted counsellors is like tearing off cap and robes, 'pulling out the roots and blocking the source'.
story.zh: 《左传·昭公九年》：“我在伯父，犹衣服之有冠冕，木水之有本原，民人之有谋主也。伯父若裂冠毁冕，拔本塞原，专弃谋主，虽戎狄其何有余一人？”

usage.en: Read 塞 as sè (to block), not sāi. Meaning shifts with context: eradicating a problem (good) or ruining a base (bad).
usage.zh: “塞”读 sè，不读 sāi。语义随语境：根治祸患为褒，毁坏根基为贬。

natural: a hundred halts, layers of calluses

meaning.en: To travel a long way with great hardship, feet thick with calluses.
meaning.zh: 走了很远的路，多次住宿，脚上磨出层层老茧，形容长途跋涉、不辞劳苦。

examples.zh: 他百舍重茧，千里迢迢赶来求教。
examples.en: He travelled a thousand li on calloused feet to seek instruction.

examples.zh: 当年他们百舍重茧，才走到了这片荒原。
examples.en: They had trudged here through countless hardships to reach this wilderness.

story.en: Mozi, hearing that Gongshu Ban was building siege engines for Chu, walked day and night for ten days, with calluses on his feet, to stop him.
story.zh: 《战国策·宋卫策》载墨子闻公输般为楚造云梯，“百舍重茧”而往见之。

usage.en: Praises determination in a long trek, often to seek a teacher or a cause. 重 is chóng; 茧 is jiǎn.
usage.zh: 赞叹为远行求学或求事而不辞艰苦；“重”读 chóng，“茧”读 jiǎn。

natural: broken willow and withered flowers

meaning.en: A faded or discarded woman; an old and derogatory image of a woman past her prime or of dubious reputation.
meaning.zh: 凋败的柳树和残败的花，旧时用来比喻失去青春、被抛弃或名声不好的女子，带有贬低。

examples.zh: 旧小说里常把失宠的妃子写成败柳残花。
examples.en: Old novels often portrayed a fallen concubine as a faded flower.

examples.zh: 这种败柳残花的说法带有偏见，今天已不宜使用。
examples.en: Describing a woman as a withered flower is prejudiced and best avoided today.

usage.en: Demeaning and sexist in tone; seen mainly in old literature. Learners should recognise it rather than use it.
usage.zh: 含轻蔑和性别偏见，主要见于旧文学；学习者了解即可，不宜使用。

natural: the dining-companion chancellor

meaning.en: An official who holds high rank but does nothing and merely accompanies others at meals.
meaning.zh: 指占着高位却无所作为、只会陪着吃饭的官员。

examples.zh: 他当了多年副手，不过是个伴食宰相。
examples.en: After years as deputy he was merely a figurehead.

examples.zh: 别让董事会变成伴食宰相的聚会。
examples.en: Don't let the board become a gathering of do-nothing dignitaries.

story.en: Tang chancellor Lu Huaishen, aware he was no match for his colleague Yao Chong, deferred to him on everything, and was nicknamed the 'dining-companion chancellor'.
story.zh: 卢怀慎与姚崇同为宰相，自以为才不及崇，事皆推让，时人称为“伴食宰相”。

usage.en: Mocks officials or executives who lack real power or effort; noun, used of people.
usage.zh: 讽刺有职无权或无所作为的官员、管理者；多指人。

literal: lean on · other people · door · house
natural: lean on another's door

meaning.en: To depend on others for one's livelihood, lacking independence.
meaning.zh: 依赖别人过活，没有独立性。

examples.zh: 他不愿傍人门户，宁愿白手起家。
examples.en: He refused to live off others and preferred to start from nothing.

examples.zh: 长期傍人门户，终究不是办法。
examples.en: Depending on others for ever is no solution.

usage.en: Often paired with 仰人鼻息; also used in literature for imitating others' style (derogatory).
usage.zh: 常与“仰人鼻息”同用；在文论中也指模仿别人，含贬义。

natural: carry cloth to trade for silk

meaning.en: Originally, trading cloth for silk; in the Book of Songs, a pretext for courting.
meaning.zh: 拿着布来换丝，本指做买卖，《诗经》中是借买卖为名前来求婚。

examples.zh: 故事里的小伙子抱布贸丝，其实是为了见心上人。
examples.en: In the tale, the young man came to barter cloth for silk, but really to see his sweetheart.

examples.zh: 诗中抱布贸丝的情景，反映了先秦的市集交易。
examples.en: The scene of bartering cloth for silk in the poem reflects trade in the pre-Qin marketplace.

story.en: In 'The Simple Fellow' a woman recalls how a smiling man came carrying cloth to trade for silk, but really to discuss marriage with her.
story.zh: 《诗经·卫风·氓》：“氓之蚩蚩，抱布贸丝。匪来贸丝，来即我谋。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Rare, mostly encountered in reading the Shijing; denotes barter or a courtship pretext.
usage.zh: 罕见，多见于读《诗经》；指以物易物或借买卖求婚。

natural: they are spent, we are full

meaning.en: The enemy's morale is drained while ours is at its height, the moment to strike.
meaning.zh: 对方士气衰竭，我方士气旺盛，正是出击的时机。

equivalents: strike while the enemy is exhausted

examples.zh: 对手体力耗尽，彼竭我盈，这正是反攻的时刻。
examples.en: The opponents are worn out and we are at full strength; now is the time to counter-attack.

examples.zh: 连续三局之后，彼竭我盈，胜负已明。
examples.en: After three games, they were spent and we were fresh; the outcome was clear.

story.en: At the Battle of Changshao, Cao Gui waited until the Qi drums had sounded three times, then said: 'They are spent; we are full, so we won.'
story.zh: 《左传·庄公十年》：“夫战，勇气也。一鼓作气，再而衰，三而竭。彼竭我盈，故克之。”

usage.en: Used of war, sport or any contest in which one side's energy fades. Often cited from the Battle of Changshao.
usage.zh: 用于战争、比赛等一方气势衰、一方气势盛的场合；常提及长勺之战。

natural: eat one day's food over two days

meaning.en: To be so poor that one has only one day's food for two; extreme poverty.
meaning.zh: 两天只吃一天的粮食，形容生活极为贫困。

examples.zh: 那几年他家并日而食，孩子们常常吃不饱。
examples.en: In those years his family ate one day's meal over two, and the children often went hungry.

examples.zh: 灾年里百姓并日而食，苦不堪言。
examples.en: In the famine the people made one day's food last two, wretched beyond words.

story.en: The Book of Rites describes a poor scholar who lives in a tiny house, eats one day's food over two days, and still keeps his principles toward his ruler.
story.zh: 《礼记·儒行》：“儒有一亩之宫，环堵之室……易衣而出，并日而食，上答之，不敢以疑；上不答，不敢以谄。”

usage.en: Formal, depicts severe poverty; often with 衣不蔽体 or 食不果腹.
usage.zh: 正式书面语，描写极度贫困；常与“衣不蔽体”“食不果腹”并用。
